messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain that drive muscle tone and spasm, which allows tight, overactive muscles to relax. It acts within the central nervous system, primarily at the level of the brain stem, and does not act on the muscles themselves or at the junction between nerves and muscle. 1,2 Because cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease, such as cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease. 1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known. Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types, including serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors. 3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, which explains several of its side effects (such as drowsiness and dry mouth) and some of its most important drug interactions. 1,2
Triples: [["Cyclobenzaprine", "has mechanism of action", "reducing nerve signals in the brain that drive muscle tone and spasm"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "allows", "tight, overactive muscles to relax"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "acts within", "central nervous system"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "primarily acts at", "brain stem"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "does not act on", "muscles themselves"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "does not act at", "junction between nerves and muscle"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "will not relieve", "muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "will not relieve", "muscle spasm caused by cerebral palsy"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "will not relieve", "muscle spasm caused by spinal cord disease"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has mechanism of action in", "fibromyalgia"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "serotonin (5-HT2A) receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "histamine receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks", "muscarinic receptor"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "is chemically related to", "tricyclic antidepressants"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "is chemically related to", "amitriptyline"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "explains", "side effect of drowsiness"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "explains", "side effect of dry mouth"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "explains", "important drug interactions"]]
Relations: ["acts within", "allows", "blocks", "does not act at", "does not act on", "explains", "has mechanism of action", "has mechanism of action in", "is chemically related to", "primarily acts at", "will not relieve"]
Answer:

completion:
acts within: The subject drug exerts its effects within the anatomical or physiological system specified by the object entity.  
allows: The subject drug enables the physiological process or state specified by the object entity to occur.  
blocks: The subject drug inhibits or prevents the function of the receptor or pathway specified by the object entity.  
does not act at: The subject drug does not exert its effects at the anatomical or physiological location specified by the object entity.  
does not act on: The subject drug does not exert its effects on the anatomical or physiological entity specified by the object entity.  
explains: The subject drug is responsible for or associated with the characteristic or effect specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug functions through the physiological or biochemical process specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action in: The subject drug functions through the physiological or biochemical process specified by the object entity in the context of the specified condition or disease.  
is chemically related to: The subject drug shares a chemical structure or origin with the compound or class of compounds specified by the object entity.  
primarily acts at: The subject drug exerts its primary effects at the anatomical or physiological location specified by the object entity.  
will not relieve: The subject drug is ineffective in alleviating or treating the condition or symptom specified by the object entity.
